key_insight: Quantum generative models can learn a Langevin potential instead of circuit rotations, using Fokker–Planck solvers to encode and sample its stationary distribution.
engineering_relevance: This physics-informed approach offers a route to trainable quantum models for scientific distributions, with efficient block encodings and analyzed circuit resources.
method: Parameterize the potential governing a Langevin process.
Hermitianize the Fokker–Planck equation and solve it using cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation.
Encode the square root of the stationary density and sample via computational-basis measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter recovery for multivariate distributions and sample-efficient, convex optimization for in-distribution targets, independent of problem dimensionality.
watch_item: The stated optimization guarantees concern in-distribution targets; performance on strongly correlated scientific data and practical hardware remains to be established.
paper_title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
